summary: A public user-posted TikTok video reportedly shows two separate phones, each running ChatGPT Advanced Voice Mode, responding to the same human speaker in one conversational environment. Both assistants reportedly responded to the shared human input rather than visibly yielding to one another or following a coordinated turn-taking process.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Two ChatGPT Advanced Voice Mode instances reportedly responded to one human input without shared speaker, yielding or conversational-floor state, directly satisfying the FC-000056 mechanism if the reported occurrence facts are accurate.

assessment_boundaries: The occurrence remains based on a public user report and is not treated as a platform-wide prevalence finding.
The complete audiovisual interaction has not been independently reconstructed; VIGIL does not infer undocumented timing or networking mechanisms.
The separate AP voice-mode article is product context only and is not occurrence corroboration.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The preserved user report describes two ChatGPT Advanced Voice Mode instances on separate devices responding to the same human input in one conversational environment. The record supports the bounded multi-participant observation but does not independently establish full timing, latency or platform-internal coordination state.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The governance issue is shared interaction arbitration. Each assistant can be individually functioning while the combined environment fails because neither instance has authoritative shared state for who owns the conversational floor, whether another synthetic participant is already responding, or which device the human intended to address. Multi-agent interaction therefore needs environment-level coordination in addition to per-agent turn-taking.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000010 shows why multi-agent safety cannot be reduced to the quality of each model response. Where several synthetic participants can observe one human input, the execution fabric needs explicit participant identity, floor ownership, yielding and conflict-resolution semantics.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Resolve the reported two-agent interaction into the shared-floor and arbitration invariants protected by FC-000056.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Two voice assistants reportedly responded to the same human utterance.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A shared conversational environment needs one authoritative representation of floor ownership before multiple synthetic responses become operative.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Both assistants acted on one utterance without an evidenced shared arbitration state.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The assistants were running on separate devices while participating in the same human conversation.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Participant coordination cannot rely only on local device state when several agents share the same social interaction surface.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The failure occurs at the interaction fabric: each local assistant can be valid while the combined system lacks cross-participant yielding and conflict resolution.
